title: Aeolus adapter regtest for backpressure and partial-JSON resilience
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: build an automated regression harness ('Aeolus adapter') that stresses the streaming/toolcall code-paths with simulated backpressure, interrupted frames, and partial NDJSON/JSON fragments to validate our recovery heuristics and backwards-compatible behavior across runtime versions. The harness will exercise: 1) continuous multiplexed streaming with interleaved toolcall messages, 2) deliberate socket write stalls and reconnects to reproduce real-world backpressure, 3) truncated/partial JSON chunks to ensure our parser fallback heuristics (schema-anchoring, incremental-parse + best-effort repair) behave consistently, and 4) compatibility fallbacks to model variants when streaming truncation would otherwise break structured output expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Aeolus harness runs as a CI job and completes within 25 minutes on the standard smoke worker
For 1000 golden seeds the harness produces identical structured-output fingerprints across runtime-1.19 and runtime-1.20 except for documented permitted diffs
When simulated socket backpressure exceeds threshold, the runtime triggers model-variant fallback and reports metric 'stream.adapter.fallback' in telemetry
Partial-JSON repair routines recover a valid top-level schema in >= 95% of truncated-frames test cases; failures are recorded as reproducible seeds
All new failures produce a tagged reproducer file checked into the regtest-artifacts bucket and create a JIRA/Linear bug with reproducer link
design_notes: We will implement the adapter as a lightweight harness that can run both locally and in CI. Key components: 1) seed corpus generator (mix of natural prompts and synthetic edge cases), 2) network emulator to inject latency/jitter/backpressure and to close streams mid-frame, 3) a verifier that validates both streaming token sequence invariants and reconstructed JSON schema, 4) a fingerprinting component that serializes normalized structured outputs for cross-runtime diffs. We'll reuse existing golden-seed formats but add a new header that contains 'latebound-recovery' flags to classify expected behavior. Decision: start with non-privileged smoke workers; later add a Dedicated GPU run for full end-to-end throughput regression. Trade-offs: aggressive repair heuristics could mask real regressions — tests must therefore surface repaired vs unrepaired cases separately.
test_matrix_rows: Transport: HTTP/1.1 streaming vs HTTP/2 vs WebSockets
Toolcall shape: single-tool single-call, multi-tool interleaved, nested function-calls
Failure mode: backpressure pause, socket close mid-json, reordered packets, token drop
Model family: small open-quantized, medium unquantized, large-llama-like variants
ci_integration: Implementation plan: 1) Add a new workflow 'aeolus-regress' in .github/workflows that runs shardable jobs (shard by seed range). 2) Integrate with existing regtest infra to upload artifacts to regtest-artifacts S3 and to create an automated issue when regressions exceed an SLA. 3) Add flakiness heuristics: a test must fail 3 consecutive runs before blocking the main branch. 4) Expose lightweight dashboard tiles in Console QA workspace with counts for 'recovered' vs 'failed' reconstructions.
implementation_steps: proto: implement network emulator and backpressure knobs (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/aeolus/pull/112)
seed corpus: author 2k mixed prompts and 200 synthetic truncation cases
verifier: extend fingerprinting lib to handle incremental-json and canonicalize ordering
ci: add workflow and shard runner scripts; set time budget and artifact upload
observability: emit metrics and add tracing spans; create Console tile for runs
risks: Repair heuristics may produce false positives and hide legit regressions
CI time/compute cost could spike if we run full suite for every PR
Edgecases on HTTP/2 flow control might be non-deterministic across platforms
mitigations: Separate 'repair' vs 'strict' test variants and require both to pass for blocking failures
Shard tests and only run full corpus on nightly and release branches
Run flaky seeds multiple times and surface seed-level flakiness in dashboard
